title: Adequate moduli morphisms are universally surjective and closed on point spaces
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $\mathcal X$ be an algebraic stack over $k$, let $Y$ be an algebraic space over $k$, and let $\phi:\mathcal X\to Y$ be an adequate moduli space in the sense of [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space]. For every $k$-scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] and every morphism $T\to Y$, form the $2$-fibre product $\mathcal X_T=\mathcal X\times_Y T$. The point space of an algebraic stack consists of field-valued objects modulo isomorphism after common field extension; a subset is open, respectively closed, when its inverse image in a smooth surjective scheme atlas is open, respectively closed. Then the induced map $|\mathcal X_T|\to|T|$ is surjective and sends every closed subset of $|\mathcal X_T|$ to a closed subset of $|T|$. No Noetherian, finite-type, reducedness or flatness hypothesis on $T\to Y$ is imposed.

source.place: Published version, Theorem 5.3.1(1),(2), printed p.511, with Proposition 5.2.9(3); primary PDF read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: First prove surjectivity for every adequate moduli space $p:\mathcal U\to V$ over $k$. For a point $v$ choose a representative $\operatorname{Spec}L\to V$. Apply [lem-sfb-adequate-base-change-affinization] to this map. Its intermediate space is $H=\operatorname{Spec}B$ over the field $L$, and $|H|\to|\operatorname{Spec}L|$ is a homeomorphism; thus $H$ is nonempty and $B\ne0$ by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The adequate map $a:\mathcal U_L\to H$ has $\mathcal O_H\simeq a_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal U_L}$ by condition (1) of [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space]. Evaluating on the affine scheme $H$ gives $B\simeq\Gamma(\mathcal U_L,\mathcal O)$, with the direct-image convention of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. If $\mathcal U_L$ had no points it would be the empty stack (an atlas would be empty), and this section ring would be the zero ring: sections are compatible families over only empty scheme objects. This contradicts $B\ne0$. A point of $\mathcal U_L$ projects to a point over $v$, proving surjectivity. Algebraicity of all fibre products used here follows from [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products].

source.place: Theorem 5.3.1(1), printed p.511; nonemptiness argument using Proposition 5.2.9(3) expanded; read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Next prove closedness for every adequate $p:\mathcal U\to V$. A closed subset $C\subseteq|\mathcal U|$ is $|\mathcal Z|$ for a reduced algebraic closed substack by [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets]. Apply [lem-sfb-adequate-closed-substack-affinization]: $\mathcal Z\to E$ is adequate, $|E|\to|W|$ is a homeomorphism, and $W\hookrightarrow V$ is closed. Step 1 applies to this adequate map as well, so its image is all of $|E|$. Consequently $p(C)=|W|$, a closed subset of $|V|$: [lem-sfb-stack-closed-immersion-calculus] makes the closed immersion $W\hookrightarrow V$ a homeomorphism onto a closed subset. This uses the actual closed-subspace inclusion in the factorization, not just a claim about dense images.

source.place: Theorem 5.3.1(2), printed p.511, closedness before base change, using Lemma 5.2.11; read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: For the given arbitrary scheme map $T\to Y$, [lem-sfb-adequate-base-change-affinization] factors $\mathcal X_T\to T$ as an adequate map $a:\mathcal X_T\to H$ followed by a map $h:H\to T$ inducing a homeomorphism on point spaces. Steps 1 and 2 were proved for every adequate moduli space with an algebraic-space target, so $|a|$ is surjective and sends closed subsets to closed subsets. A homeomorphism is surjective and sends closed subsets to closed subsets (use continuity of its inverse); therefore $|h|\circ|a|$ has both properties. This proves the item for all $T$, including the empty scheme, without claiming that $\mathcal X_T\to T$ itself is adequate.

source.place: Theorem 5.3.1(2), final sentence of its closedness proof, printed p.511, using Proposition 5.2.9(3); read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

lean.statement: theorem adequateModuli_universal_closed_topology {k : Type u} [Field k] (F : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))) (hF : IsAlgebraicModuliStack F) (Y : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (φ : BasedFunctor F (discreteModuli Y.obj.obj)) (hφ : IsAdequateModuliSpace F hF Y φ) : ∀ (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (t : yoneda.obj T ⟶ Y.obj.obj), Function.Surjective (moduliPointMap (moduliTwoFiberSnd φ (discreteModuliMap t))) ∧ IsClosedMap (moduliPointMap (moduliTwoFiberSnd φ (discreteModuliMap t)))
lean.note: The actual second projection from the 2-fibre product is a surjective closed map. The target is the point space of the discrete groupoid of T, canonically homeomorphic to the Zariski space of T by stack_point_topology, with the residue-field characterization in that theorem. No base-change adequacy hypothesis is imposed.
